narration: Look! A point.
Woah! It drew a shape.
Let's look at this shape closely.
There are no gaps in its boundary.
Is it open or closed?
Is this shape open or closed?
What about this one?
And this?
How about this one?
These two shapes are open...
...and these two shapes are closed.
Look! The boundaries of the shapes are different too.
Some are straight and some are curved.
Which boundaries are straight and which are curved?
You got it! These boundaries are straight, while these are curved.
Tap the figure that is both closed and made of straight lines.
We call this a polygon.
A closed figure made of only straight line segments is called a polygon.
Which of these figures are polygons?
These line segments are the sides of the polygon.
The point where two sides meet is called a vertex.
When two sides meet, they also form an angle.
Label the parts of the polygon.
How many sides does this polygon have?
This polygon has 5 sides.
Now let's change how it looks.
Drag any vertex. Stretch it, squash it, or resize it.
Whoa! It looks quite different now.
Its appearance has completely changed.
But not everything has changed.
Let's count the sides again.
Both polygons still have 5 sides.
So the number of sides gives us a good way to name polygons.
A polygon with 3 sides is called a triangle.
A polygon with 4 sides is called a quadrilateral.
Select all the quadrilaterals.
A polygon with 5 sides is called a pentagon.
A polygon with 6 sides is called a hexagon.
A polygon with 7 sides is called a heptagon.
A polygon with 8 sides is called an octagon.
Let's recall the different types of polygons we learnt about.
Which of these is a polygon?
Classify the figures as a polygon or not a polygon.
Find the odd one out. Which figure is NOT a polygon?
Which of these is a pentagon?
Classify each figure as a hexagon or a heptagon.
You did it! Now you know what makes a figure a polygon.
